title: The Title Chain and the Twelve-Year Pairs
subtitle: Who held the paper and who held the land at Cedwyn / Tŷ Mawr (Llandough and Leckwith), 1841–1987, each step tied to its catalogue entry
note: Ingredients and citations, not conclusions. Pattern charts are for discussion; dates come from the cited records; nothing here is a finding of any court.
court_first: Court of Appeal, 31 Jul 1987 (EV-0080): the court found Mary and Frederick Buckler in adverse possession of the farmhouse from 2 Feb 1955.
The court held that the 11 Dec 1962 possession order could be enforced for 12 years, to Dec 1974, and kept the paper title alive until then.

The court held that the two letters of 31 Oct 1974 made Mary a licensee, because she did not reject them in writing; on that basis it treated twelve years of adverse possession as never completed and treated BP as owner.
The court called the one-sided licence point "a new one" and noted the risk of an owner keeping title alive "for very many years until it suits him to evict".

Mary Williams’s assertion that the family owned the farmhouse outright was never tried: her documents were not produced, and BP Pension Trust’s 1974 action, in which she pleaded ownership, was never relisted. BP Properties’ position on the register rests on first registration as proprietor in 1982/83; whether her case was before HM Land Registry then is not shown in the records held.

catalogue_new.summary: Shows each dated pair on one 1870–1990 timeline with its exact gap: 1926→1938 12y 11m 24d; 1939→1952 13y 4m 22d; 1949→1961 12y 1m 27d; 1962→1974 11y 10m 20d; 1974→1986 11y 8m 24d.
catalogue_new.limits: A gap of about twelve years is not itself evidence of intent. Across 34 dated events, 12-year gaps occur about as often as 11- and 13-year gaps (17, 12 and 15 pairs).

catalogue_new.title: Bute Glamorgan manorial records: court books to 1937, extinguishment of manorial incidents 1929–40, Ministry of Agriculture correspondence 1938, steward for the "Glamorgan manors of Mountjoy Ltd" 1937 (Glamorgan Archives DB/M/1–21)
catalogue_new.label: ARCHIVE CATALOGUE ENTRIES — DOCUMENTS NOT YET SEEN
catalogue_new.status: PENDING — view free at Glamorgan Archives.
catalogue_new.summary: Bute’s manorial titles in Glamorgan were being wound down after 1 Jan 1926, when the Law of Property Act 1922 turned copyhold into freehold (EV-0616); in 1938, the year of the sale to Western Ground Rents (deed not examined), Bute’s estate was corresponding with the Ministry about extinguishing manorial incidents.
catalogue_new.limits: No record yet shows that any part of Great House Farm was copyhold of Llandough manor after 1900.

catalogue_new.title: Mountjoy Ltd in the Bute estate catalogue: "In 1926, the remaining Bute property was incorporated under a private family company called Mountjoy Ltd" (TNA Discovery, GB 0214 DB administrative history)
catalogue_new.date: 1926 per the catalogue (company formed May 1922, EV-0624); 1938 sale
catalogue_new.label: ARCHIVE CATALOGUE TEXT
catalogue_new.status: READ (catalogue text); company records not yet seen.
catalogue_new.summary: Names Mountjoy Ltd as the Bute family company from 1926 and records that in 1938 Mountjoy sold its leasehold interests. Mountjoy Ltd is named as the seller to Western Ground Rents in 1938 in press reports (EV-0022); the 1938 deed has not been examined.
catalogue_new.limits: Press of May 1922 shows the company was formed in 1922 (EV-0624), so 1926 reads as the year further property was brought in. The 1987 judgment does not mention Mountjoy; it goes from "the Marquis" (1916) to WGR (1938). No Llandough-juxta-Penarth instrument in the DBDT catalogue names Mountjoy.

catalogue_new.title: London Gazette, 29 October 1926, p.7040: release of the liquidator of Lewis & Pritchard Ltd, quarry firm ("surplus plant at Llandough" sold Aug 1925)
catalogue_new.label: PUBLISHED RECORD
catalogue_new.summary: The quarry firm working at Llandough was wound up by 1926.
catalogue_new.limits: Whose land the firm worked, and on what terms, is not stated.

catalogue_new.title: Law of Property Act 1922, ss.128 and 138: all copyhold enfranchised into freehold from 1 January 1926; manorial incidents to be extinguished within ten years
catalogue_new.label: LAW — ENACTED TEXT
catalogue_new.summary: 1 Jan 1926 rebuilt English property law and reached Bute’s manors directly. A copyholder’s land became the holder’s freehold by statute.
catalogue_new.limits: Whether the family’s holding was ever copyhold is not shown in any record on file.

catalogue_new.title: The twelve-year rule for land: Real Property Limitation Act 1874 (from 1 January 1879), restated by the Limitation Act 1939 (in force 1 July 1940)
catalogue_new.label: LAW — ENACTED TEXT AND STANDARD SOURCES
catalogue_new.summary: Twelve years had applied to actions to recover land since 1 Jan 1879; the 1939 Act restated it. So the 18 May 1939 Parcel B letting (EV-0023) was made while a twelve-year rule was already in force. While a written tenancy runs, the tenant’s years do not count against the landlord. A mere visit or assertion does not stop time (1939 Act s.13, quoted in the judgment).
catalogue_new.limits: The 1940 Act did not introduce the twelve-year period for land; it restated it.

catalogue_new.title: Press, 1904–05: Cardiff’s Western Sewer Sub-committee completes the conveyance of the pumping-station site and sewer easements from the representatives of Lord Bute (Evening Express 23 Mar 1905; Weekly Mail 11 Jun 1904)
catalogue_new.label: PUBLISHED RECORD — NEWSPAPER TEXT
catalogue_new.status: READ (newspaper text). The deed itself is not yet copied.
catalogue_new.summary: Cardiff paid £5,362 7s for Bute easements over about 2½ miles of sewer route (1904) and completed the conveyance of the pumping-station site and easements in early 1905. This fits EV-0013 being the Western District outfall sewer easements.
catalogue_new.limits: Until the 23 Feb 1905 deed is copied, its land and terms are not confirmed; an alternative reading is a Leckwith reservoir main.

catalogue_new.title: Covenant wording: Western Ground Rents’ Llandough covenant of 5 March 1962 and BP’s covenant of 23 May 1975, side by side
catalogue_new.label: RECORD COMPARISON — FROM REGISTER ENTRIES AND A RECITED CONVEYANCE
catalogue_new.summary: The 1975 covenant repeats the 1962 estate wording almost word for word: the benefit of the seller’s land "within a radius of one hundred yards"; the same banned uses ("noisy noxious or offensive trade … public worship … lunatic asylum … public house inn tavern or beer-shop … advertisement"); and the same proviso that the covenant is not "evidence of a building scheme". BP’s 1975 deed was drafted from the Western Ground Rents estate precedent.
catalogue_new.limits: Shared wording shows continuity of drafting and estate management after BP bought Western Ground Rents in 1969 (EV-0288); it is silent on anyone’s intentions.

catalogue_new.title: 23 May 1975: conveyance of the farmhouse plot and other land, BP Pension Trust to BP Properties; the rest kept as "Retained Land"
catalogue_new.label: REGISTER ENTRY — DEED NOT HELD
catalogue_new.status: PENDING — the deed is on the HM Land Registry file.
catalogue_new.summary: The register records a conveyance inside the BP group six months before the Vale of Glamorgan became a compulsory registration area (1 Dec 1975, EV-0265), so this conveyance triggered no registration.
catalogue_new.limits: The deed’s plan and recitals have not been read.

catalogue_new.title: Root of title: the 25 December 1938 conveyance, and why the 31 December 1969 sale fell under the 30-year rule (LPA 1925 s.44(1); LPA 1969 ss.23, 31(2))
catalogue_new.label: LAW — ENACTED TEXT, APPLIED TO RECORDS ON FILE
catalogue_new.summary: The cut from a 30-year to a 15-year root applied only to contracts made after 1 Jan 1970, so the 31 Dec 1969 WGR → BP Pension Trust sale needed a root before Dec 1939: in practice the 25 Dec 1938 conveyance (known from recitals; the deed has not been examined), then 31 years 6 days old. In 1965 the school-site contract had to contract out of the 30-year rule to start from the same 1938 deed. BP’s 1969 and 1971 abstracts (EV-0043, EV-0045) should therefore begin with the 1938 deed and show what it conveyed at Llandough.
catalogue_new.limits: Starting title at a purchase from a great estate was common practice.

catalogue_new.title: Crichel Down rules and military land: what applies at Llandough, and three unread files (TNA MAF 11/1022, HLG 23/17384, MH 96/291)
catalogue_new.label: LEADS — FILES NOT YET SEEN
catalogue_new.status: PENDING — order or view at Kew.
catalogue_new.summary: The Crichel Down rules cover surplus land a public body bought under compulsion and offer it back to the former freeholder. MAF 11/1022 is dated two days after Mrs M. D. Buckler called the losses "a Welsh case of Crichel Down" (EV-0037).
catalogue_new.limits: No requisition of this farm, and no Air Ministry or airfield taking of it, has been found on file. Where public bodies took land nearby, the party of record was Bute, Mountjoy, WGR or a developer.

catalogue_new.title: Financial Times full text, June 1983 – September 1986 (885 issues): no item on Llandough, Great House Farm, Tŷ Mawr, BP Properties / BP Pension Trust, Western Ground Rents or the case
catalogue_new.label: SEARCH RECORD — NOTHING FOUND
catalogue_new.summary: The national financial press of the period carried no report of the case or the land.
catalogue_new.limits: Absence from one newspaper is not evidence about the case itself.

catalogue_new.title: Mountjoy Ltd formed in May 1922 as the 4th Marquess of Bute’s estate company (£1,000,000; named after his title Viscount Mountjoy); lord of Llandough court leet in 1932
catalogue_new.label: PUBLISHED RECORD — NEWSPAPER TEXT (SEARCH-RESULT TEXT, PAGE IMAGES NOT SEEN)
catalogue_new.summary: Mountjoy Ltd was formed in May 1922 with £1,000,000 capital "to take over Lord Bute’s life interest in all the estates in South Wales and Scotland" and traded as "Mountjoy, Limited (Bute Estate, Cardiff)". In 1932 "the annual court leet dinner given by Mountjoy Estate, Ltd." was held at the Merry Harriers’ Hotel, Llandough. A Mountjoy Limited at Queen Anne’s Gate went into members’ voluntary winding-up in 1955 (same company probable, not proven).
catalogue_new.limits: A company taking a tenant for life’s "life interest" would not by itself hold the fee simple; who conveyed the legal estate in 1938 — Mountjoy, Bute, the settlement trustees or all of them — is a question the 1938 deed will answer.

catalogue_new.title: The 1938 sale as one transaction: contracts 17 May 1938, Western Ground Rents registered 4–5 July 1938, manors kept back, Mountjoy as mortgagee to 1944
catalogue_new.label: PUBLISHED RECORD AND CATALOGUE ENTRIES — DEED NOT READ
catalogue_new.summary: Bute sold "nearly the whole of the Mountjoy estate" to a single buyer (press). The manors, the castles and some named lands were kept back, so the manorial title of Llandough stayed with Mountjoy in 1938 (manors disposed of 1950–57, EV-0027). A Cardiff strip was reported transferred to Western Ground Rents with other Bute property the previous December (Western Mail, 14 Jun 1939). In Leckwith the lettings run Bute (1925) → Mountjoy (1934) → WGR (1944). The 25 Dec 1938 conveyance is known from recitals in later documents; the deed has not been examined.
catalogue_new.limits: No record names a second grantee under the 25 Dec 1938 deed, and none states whether Great House Farm or Parcel B was included. No DBDT Llandough-juxta-Penarth instrument names Mountjoy.

catalogue_new.title: "Cydfin Wood, Leckwith, the property of Lord Bute": Penarth police court reports, Evening Express 7 and 14 January 1903
catalogue_new.label: PUBLISHED RECORD — NEWSPAPER TEXT
catalogue_new.summary: The name Cydfin was in use for a wood in Leckwith in 1903, and the press then described it as the property of Lord Bute.
catalogue_new.limits: A police-court report is not a title document.

catalogue_new.title: Cardiff Corporation at Cedwyn, 1905–1989: one corporate body for the 1905 and 1961 rights; dealings with Western Ground Rents 1938–47; no Cardiff role found in the 1989 planning file
catalogue_new.label: RECORD SYNTHESIS — FROM REGISTER ENTRIES, PRESS AND PLANNING RECORDS
catalogue_new.summary: The County Borough of Cardiff that took rights in Feb 1905 became the City corporation in Oct 1905, so the 1905 and 1961 grantee is one body; it appears on the woodland register only as the holder of rights, never as registered proprietor (the registered proprietor of the woodland from 25 Nov 1994 is Forest of Cardiff, a company). The 1989 outline permission was granted by the Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council.
catalogue_new.limits: Nothing on file shows Cardiff granting, advising or being consulted on the 1989 application; the Vale’s consultation list would settle it.

catalogue_new.title: Authenticity audit of both title lines: which instrument has been seen, which is known only from a recital, press or catalogue (analysis, 25 Oct 2026)
catalogue_new.label: RESEARCH ARTIFACT — ANALYSIS OF CATALOGUED RECORDS
catalogue_new.summary: Every link in the paper chain from 1922 to 1983 is known only from recitals, press or catalogues; no operative instrument from it is held. The family’s records on file (c.1841 tithe, 1872–76 rate books, 1824 survey, 1916 tenancy, 1939 letting) are rent-book, rate-book and tenancy entries in the name of John Williams; the parcels they cover are not identified, and none names the Tŷ Mawr house parcel. The single most useful document is the 25 Dec 1938 conveyance with its plan. BP Properties became registered proprietor at first registration in 1982/83; whether Mary Williams’s case was before HM Land Registry then is not shown in the records held.
catalogue_new.limits: Neither side’s root is proved from a document in hand; the family’s 1987 case was possessory, not documentary.

events.detail: Mary Williams's later account dates a Bute agreement (sale or quarry lease of the house parcel) with Daniel Thomas & Son to 6 Nov 1877. The instrument has not been found; the 6 Nov 1877 lease photographed at Glamorgan Archives is a Clyde Street, Roath building lease, not the farm.
events.source: EV-0006, EV-0008 (Mary Williams's account); EV-0213 (the Roath lease)

events.detail: 23 Feb 1905: Bute conveys rights over a strip of what is now the woodland title to Cardiff County Borough. It is very probably the sewer/pumping-station easement Cardiff paid for; the deed itself is unread.
events.source: WA735527 Charges entry 1 (register view 18 Sep 2026); EV-0013; cycle-038 report

events.detail: Feb 1916: the court records a yearly tenancy of "the whole of the farm" to John Williams from "the Marquis". It is the first record that puts the family’s occupation on a tenancy footing.

1 Jan 1926: Law of Property Act 1922 s.128 turns all copyhold into freehold; the 1925 property Acts come into force. The same year Bute's remaining property is put into Mountjoy Ltd, the company that sold to WGR in 1938 (month of incorporation not yet confirmed). Llandough Rectory, beside "part of the Bute Estate", is sold 7 Oct 1926. Press of May 1922 shows Mountjoy Ltd was in fact formed in 1922 (EV-0624); the catalogue’s 1926 reads as the year further property was brought in.
events.source: LPA 1922 ss.128, 138; TNA catalogue GB 0214 DB (F043); Glamorgan Archives DSA/12/5085 (catalogue); EV-0624

events.detail: Dec 1926: Bute lets land near Lewis Road, Llandough, to Penarth Urban District Council. Catalogue entry only; the plan has not been matched to farm fields.
10 Nov 1925: the Llandough quarry / lime works plant is catalogued and sold (Lewis & Pritchard's "surplus plant at Llandough" was sold Aug 1925). The quarry leaving is the end point of the 1877 bar.
events.source: Glamorgan Archives DSA/12/4888 (catalogue only); London Gazette 29 Oct 1926 p.7040

events.detail: 1928 is the year Mary Williams reported as the last rent paid for the house parcel. It rests on her account only; no rent book is on file.

25 Dec 1938 (completion reported 23 Dec): a conveyance from Mountjoy Ltd to Western Ground Rents Ltd is recited in later documents; the deed has not been examined, so whether it covered Parcel B is not known. The 1965 school sale uses it as root of title.

18 May 1939: WGR lets 5.30 acres (Parcel B) beside Ty-Mawr farmhouse to John Williams, then about 72, monthly at 8s, "reserving quarrying rights". While a tenancy runs, the tenant's years do not count against the landlord.
events.source: Glamorgan Archives DBDT/123/7; EV-0023; archive reply ref 2026/4439

events.detail: 2 Feb 1949: John Williams's tenancy is surrendered after arrears and an unwritten yearly tenancy is granted to Frederick Buckler.
10 Oct 1952: WGR's agents write that they "did not propose to proceed with the letting to Mr Frederick Buckler". Last rent follows in 1953, under a judgment for arrears.
4 Jul 1955: a High Court possession order is enforced on all the farm except the farmhouse and garden (notice to quit expired 2 Feb 1955).

19 Nov 1958: Mrs M. D. Buckler tells Glamorgan County Council's planning committee the land was "wrongfully appropriated" by Glamorgan CC, Penarth UDC, Cardiff RDC and WGR. Same year: Leckwith Common inquiry 6 May (she asserted grazing rights) and the Cardiff (Leckwith Common) CPO 1957 confirmed 8 Sep; no petition was lodged.
events.source: EV-0037 (Western Mail 20 Nov 1958 p.7, OCR); EV-0035; EV-0038; TNA BD 11/3775 (unread)

events.detail: 1959 (month unknown): WGR offers Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden; she refuses and asserts title through her grandfather.
29 Mar 1961: deed between WGR, South Western Brick & Tile Co. and Cardiff City Corporation giving rights over the "pink" land now in the woodland title. Rights, not a transfer; the deed is not held.
11 Dec 1962: Cardiff County Court possession order (farmhouse and garden) and mesne profits, WGR v Frederick and Mary Buckler. An order like this could be enforced for 12 years.
Jun 1963: suspended committal order over the mesne profits.
Mar 1965: a weekly tenancy is offered to "Mrs Williams" and refused. BP later admitted Mary was in adverse possession from 1965–67.

11 Jun 1965: WGR with Lakeside & Llandough Development Co sells the Llandough primary school site; root of title the 25 Dec 1938 conveyance. Whether the site lay in the fields repossessed in 1955 is not shown on file.

16 Jun 1970: VG41 registered under the Commons Registration Act 1965, Glamorgan County Council as registration authority, on what the wiki maps as the south-east ground of Parcel A. Notice was public only; the objection window closed in 1972.
1971: abstract of title prepared for BP Pension Trust (recited only).

31 Oct 1974: two letters from BP Properties grant Mary a rent-free licence; the warrant is withdrawn before 25 Nov. Leave to enforce the 1962 order had been obtained on 19 Sep 1974 (11y 9m 8d after it), 41 days before the 12 years ran out.
23 May 1975: BP Pension Trust conveys the farmhouse plot and other land to BP Properties, keeping the rest as "Retained Land"; six months before the Vale became a compulsory registration area.
events.source: WA735527 Charges entries 4–5; reopen-loop ground R10

events.detail: 30 Nov 1982: Linklaters & Paines apply for first registration of WA231076 for BP Properties, after a 19 Nov 1982 conveyance. BP Properties is entered as registered proprietor.
23 Feb 1983: application for WA240304 (farmhouse). Mary Williams dies 26 Mar 1983; Linklaters–HMLR correspondence follows 8 Apr 1983.
events.source: HM Land Registry letter 23 Mar 2026; reopen-loop ground R3

events.detail: 24 Jul 1986: Hollis J decides for BP Properties; the Court of Appeal dismisses the appeal on 31 Jul 1987.

rooms.title: Cedwyn before the paper
rooms.text: Tŷ Mawr alias Cedfin sat in the old manor lands of Llandough and Leckwith beside the church, its cemetery used from about 370 to 1024 and a cross of the 10th–11th century. The Williams family farmed here and kept faith with the parish around them. This room holds the place names and the oldest records.

rooms.title: The quarry and the estate
rooms.text: In 1877, as the family later recounted, the Bute estate — lords of the manor — made an agreement with Daniel Thomas & Son over the house parcel; lime kilns and quarry work followed. In 1905 Bute conveyed rights over a strip to Cardiff for the western sewer. The first piece of the land had gone to industry.

rooms.title: A tenancy on the whole farm
rooms.text: The court records that in February 1916 "the Marquis" let "the whole of the farm" to John Williams by the year. Bute’s estates had passed into his company Mountjoy Ltd in 1922; the quarry plant was sold in 1925, and on 1 January 1926 the law ended copyhold tenure.

rooms.title: Sold over their heads
rooms.text: At Christmas 1938, later documents recite, Mountjoy Ltd conveyed to Western Ground Rents Ltd; the deed itself has not been examined, and the manorial title of Llandough was kept back. Five months later Parcel B, 5.30 acres by the farmhouse, was let to John Williams, then about 72, month by month at 8s, "reserving quarrying rights". About 109 acres of Leckwith Woods went to Cardiff as a gift.

rooms.title: The fields go
rooms.text: In 1949 the tenancy passed to Frederick Buckler, unwritten. In 1952 the agents dropped the letting; the last rent was paid in 1953. On 4 July 1955 a High Court order was enforced on every field — all but the farmhouse and garden.

rooms.title: "A Welsh case of Crichel Down"
rooms.text: In 1958 Leckwith Common was taken for a playing field and Mrs M. D. Buckler stood before the county planning committee and told them the family’s land had been "wrongfully appropriated". She refused a tenancy of her own home in 1959. In 1961 rights over the woodland were granted between WGR, a brick company and Cardiff.

rooms.title: Order, school and green
rooms.text: In December 1962 the county court ordered possession of the farmhouse — an order that was then held for almost twelve years. In 1965 a school rose on 3.352 acres sold for £16,800; Mary refused a second tenancy. In 1969 BP bought Western Ground Rents, and in 1970 the green was entered on the register as VG41.

rooms.title: Two letters
rooms.text: In September 1974 leave was given to enforce the 1962 order, 41 days before its twelve years ran out; on 31 October two letters gave Mary a rent-free licence and the warrant was withdrawn. In May 1975 the farmhouse plot moved inside the BP group, six months before registration became compulsory.

rooms.title: Registered
rooms.text: In November 1982 and February 1983 BP Properties applied for first registration of the woodland and the farmhouse and was entered as registered proprietor. Mary Williams died on 26 March 1983. Whether her case was before HM Land Registry is not shown in the records held.

rooms.title: Judgment, and the record since
rooms.text: The courts found the family had held the farmhouse adversely from 1955, but held that the 1962 order and the 1974 letters kept the paper title alive, and treated BP as owner. Mary’s assertion of ownership was never tried. The charts in this room set out the dated pairs and the parcels for the visitor to weigh.

hypotheses.name: Sequential parcel capture and permission-framing (‘the Paper Siege’): separate takings, title claims, licences and registrations progressively reduced the Williams family’s standing on paper
hypotheses.explains: The 1841 occupation footprint; the separate 1939 fields letting and farmhouse claim; the 1958 Crichel Down complaint; recurring permission framing; 1974 letters; 1975 transfer; 1982–83 registrations; 1987 amalgamation; later loss of the house.
hypotheses.limits: The tithe records occupation, not ownership. Deeds and plans remain incomplete; the 1939 signature is unauthenticated; the registration files and proof of notice remain to be checked. Intentional coordination, fraud, violence and archaeological concealment are not findings. The Court of Appeal outcome remains the operative legal result.

hypotheses.name: A long private property and possession dispute, decided in the courts, followed by demolition and redevelopment, with title-root questions open
Planning and developer corner-cutting without a title scheme (1990 ground investigation, 1992 reserved matters, archaeology condition 18)
A repeated pattern of recasting occupation as permission near twelve-year limits, across successive title holders (the family’s working theory; ingredients in EV-0607 to EV-0609)
